## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Dutiyavedanā Sutta* (“Feelings [2nd]”, Iti 53) is a discourse in the *Itivuttaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya, categorized under section 3.4 and located at page 47 in the Pali Text Society edition [SuttaCentral]. The text instructs practitioners on how the three types of feeling should properly be viewed [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records nineteen modern translations across seventeen languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies passage-level parallels to the *Daṭṭhabba Sutta* of the Saṁyutta Nikāya (SN 36.5) and the *Sāriputtattheragāthā* of the Theragāthā (Thag 17.2) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus strongly corroborates the link to the *Vedanā Saṁyutta* (SN 36), recording substantial Pali-internal text reuse between Iti 53 (§§2.1–4.1) and SN 36.5 (§§5.0.3–5.3.1) at 0.93 similarity [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns shorter segments of the sutta with passages in the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45), the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), the *Chakkanipāta* (AN 6), the *Diṭṭhi Saṁyutta* (SN 24), the commentary (*Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā*), and later council texts (*Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā*) [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Itivuttaka* itself, segments 3.4–5.1 are identical with passages in both the *Nissaraṇiya Sutta* (Iti 72) and the *Asubhānupassī Sutta* (Iti 85) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language alignments with a score of 10 or greater are reported [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
